title: Integrability of averaged Gaussian indicators
statement: For every natural number $n$, every measurable set $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, and every real number $\theta$, the function $x\mapsto\int 1_A(\cos(\theta)x+\sin(\theta)y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$ is integrable with respect to standard Gaussian measure $\gamma_n$ on $\mathbb R^n$.
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. For measurable $A$ and every real $\theta$, the function $u_\theta$ is $\gamma_n$-integrable.
